body:
Fassung 0.44.36, Migrationen 143 und 144, PWA-Speicher `schaefchen-online-v118`.

## Wofür es den Bereich gibt

Nicht für „welche Verteiler haben wir" — das beantwortet die Geräteliste. Sondern für die vier Fragen, die auf der Baustelle täglich anstehen:

1. Welche Prüfung ist abgelaufen? (DGUV V3, vierteljährlich)
2. Wo muss diesen Monat die Prüftaste gedrückt werden?
3. Was steht auf dem Zähler — und was hat die Baustelle verbraucht?
4. Wo steht welcher Verteiler?

Die Liste sortiert deshalb nach Dringlichkeit statt nach Nummer, und jede Zeile trägt die Farbe ihrer schlimmeren Frist.

## Zwei Fristen, nicht eine

Der monatliche Druck auf die Prüftaste ist keine Prüfung im Sinne der DGUV V3. Er ersetzt die vierteljährliche Prüfung durch die Elektrofachkraft nicht und darf ihren Termin nicht verschieben. Migration 143 führt ihn deshalb in `power_rcd_tests` und nicht in `device_inspections` — eine Zeile dort setzt die Fälligkeit des Geräts neu, und dann verschiebt ein Tastendruck den Termin, an dem die Fachkraft anrücken muss.

Beide neuen Tabellen sind Aufzeichnungen: die API-Rolle bekommt `SELECT, INSERT` und kein `UPDATE`. Eine Korrektur ist ein neuer Eintrag, wie bei Übergaben und Prüfungen der Geräteverwaltung auch.

## Zählerstände

Anlass (Aufstellen, Zwischenablesung, Abbau) und Baustelle stehen an der Ablesung selbst: ein Verteiler wandert im Jahr über mehrere Baustellen, und die Rechnung von Baustelle drei darf sich nicht ändern, weil er inzwischen woanders steht. Ein Stand unter dem vorigen wird mit `power_meter_reading_backwards` abgewiesen statt stillschweigend gebucht — ein Zähler läuft vorwärts, und eine negative Menge fiele sonst erst dem Kunden auf.

## Wo er steht

Am Telefon als Karte unter „Maschinen & Geräte": ein Verteiler ist für den Monteur ein Gerät, und die Leiste unten hat keinen Platz für einen weiteren Eintrag. Am Rechner als eigener Punkt in der Seitenleiste.

Angelegt werden Verteiler weiterhin in der Geräteverwaltung mit der Kategorie „Baustromverteiler". Der Bereich legt nichts an und führt keine zweiten Stammdaten — er zeigt Fristen und nimmt Aufzeichnungen entgegen.

## Beim Prüfen gefunden und behoben

- **Migration 143 hatte einen Teil der Anlagefunktion verloren.** Sie schreibt `seed_device_master_data` neu, um die Kategorie zu ergänzen; beim ersten Anlauf fiel dabei die Voreinstellung des Lagerorts still aus dem Rumpf. Gemeldet hat es die Abnahme von 095; die Abnahme von 143 hält jetzt namentlich fest, was im Rumpf stehenbleiben muss.
- **Die Ablesung wurde ohne Baustelle gebucht** — für die Weiterberechnung genau die Angabe, auf die es ankommt. Sie kommt jetzt vom Gerät, wenn keine angegeben ist. Ein Test lässt einen Verteiler umziehen und prüft, dass die alte Ablesung bei der alten Baustelle bleibt.
- **Am Rechner leuchteten zwei Einträge gleichzeitig**: die Vertretung für die Telefonleiste („Baustrom" liegt dort unter „Geräte") galt auch in der Seitenleiste, wo beide Bereiche eigene Einträge haben.

## Geprüft

- Alle 144 Migrationen auf einer frischen Datenbank, zweimal hintereinander (Idempotenz), danach Seeds und **alle SQL-Abnahmen grün**
- **130 API-Tests grün** mit PostgreSQL-Integration, Mindestabdeckung eingehalten (`power.mjs`: 94 % Zeilen)
- **106 Frontend-Tests plus Smoke-Test grün**
- Im Browser durchgespielt: Karte am Telefon (420 px) und Leisteneintrag am Rechner (1280 px), FI-Test gebucht und nachgewiesen, dass die Prüffrist stehenbleibt, Zählerstand mit Verbrauchsangabe, Rückwärtsstand abgewiesen, kein waagerechtes Scrollen in beiden Breiten

body:
Closes three debt items left behind by the build-time commit-hash feature (PR #77). Six commits, each reviewable alone.

## 1 — the DI contract is a type, not a string

`AndroidPlatformModule` bound `named(COMMIT_HASH_QUALIFIER)` and `AppNavHost` read it back. A shared constant made a *rename* compile-safe, but a retyped literal at either site compiled, passed the whole gate, and crashed the app at launch.

It is now a `CommitHash` type, bound and resolved by type. There is no string left to misspell.

Stated narrowly on purpose: this stops a **typo**, not a **rewrite**. `koinInject<String>()` written at that line still compiles green and still crashes at launch, and nothing observes it — closing that would need a Compose-runtime test `:ui-android` does not have. The code comment says exactly this rather than claiming the two sides "cannot disagree".

The type lives in `presentation/src/androidMain`. It went to `commonMain` first, and the review caught that: producer and consumer are both Android-only, so `androidMain` keeps it out of the Kotlin/Native compilation entirely — which deleted eleven lines of KDoc that existed only to explain why a `@JvmInline value class` never reaches the exported Obj-C surface. Verified against the artifact, not the exit code: `CommitHash` appears zero times in all three generated `JustChillKit.h` files, while `SupabaseConfig` appears eight.

Side effect: `hh/profile/CommitHashUi.kt` is down to one reason to change, closing a fourth debt item.

## 2 — the convention plugin is idiomatic Gradle

`BuildInfoConventionPlugin` declared no marker for the AGP application plugin and called `extensions.configure<ApplicationAndroidComponentsExtension>` eagerly inside `apply()`, so it depended on the order of the `plugins { }` block. Now: marker declared, and the body deferred behind `pluginManager.withPlugin("com.android.application")`.

Proven in both directions. With the old code, moving `id("justchill.build.info")` above the AGP alias fails with `Extension of type 'ApplicationAndroidComponentsExtension' does not exist`. With the new code, the same reorder builds and generates correctly.

Deferring cost the loud failure, so it was restored deliberately: applying the plugin to a non-application module now fails with `The justchill.build.info plugin generates BuildInfo.kt through the Android APPLICATION variant API, but :domain never applied 'com.android.application', so nothing was registered and no BuildInfo.kt exists.` A second silent path — `variant.sources.kotlin?.` skipping the source-directory wiring — is now a `checkNotNull`.

## 3 — `build-logic` has tests, and they are on the gate

`normalizeCommitHash` is the only barrier between `git rev-parse HEAD` and a Kotlin string literal, and it had no test — `build-logic` had no test source set at all. It now has nine cases covering the accept path, uppercase normalisation, whitespace, and rejection of quotes, backslashes, `$`, newlines, a `-dirty` suffix and the empty string.

`:build-logic:test` runs under `./gradlew qualityGate`, named explicitly on the root project because an included build is unreachable by task-name matching. Configuration cache still reuses across runs.

One of those tests closes a debt item that a comment had declared unclosable: it pins the `"unknown"` sentinel's spelling with a literal assertion, the same technique the `:ui-android` side already used. Both sides are now pinned by a test that spells the word out.

## Verification

`./gradlew qualityGate --rerun-tasks` green from scratch, 245 tasks, including the macOS-only iOS compile and link. `./gradlew assembleDevDebug` green. Every claim above was proven by running the mutation and checking which test went red, not by inspection.

## Review history

Writer → Opus reviewer → fix, then Judgment Day: two blind Opus judges, a bounded fix round, and an independent final verification that re-ran every mutation itself. Zero `CRITICAL`, zero contradictions between judges.

The final verification returned `ESCALATED` on documentation only — the commit that moved `CommitHash` left `PROGRESS.md` still naming `commonMain`, and re-stated in a module doc the exact kind of unbacked "nothing catches this" claim that one of the ledger items existed to kill. Those six lines are fixed in the last commit.

## Debt still open, recorded in `docs/PROGRESS.md`

- `generate()`'s string template has no test: deleting the quotes around the interpolated value reddens nothing in `build-logic`. Closing it needs a `ProjectBuilder`/`GradleRunner` invocation against a temp dir. Chosen omission, not an oversight.
- `build-logic` is on the gate for its tests only and applies no detekt, so its own sources are the one body of code the gate runs and never lints.
- Nothing observes what `AppNavHost` asks for; see the narrowing in section 1.

Segunda vuelta sobre el color, tras ver el deploy de Netlify.

## Qué cambia

Un solo token: `--accent-soft` pasa de `#3090c0` a `#369fd2`.

```diff
+  --accent-soft: #369fd2;
```

En la ronda anterior (#2) rederivé la paleta al tono del azul de Canva de Virginia, pero oscureciendo cada nivel lo justo para cumplir WCAG AA. Al ver el resultado desplegado, sigue viendo demasiado oscuros los títulos de sección y pide su `#369fd2` tal cual.

Promoção `dev → production` para cortar a **v1.17.1**, que aponta o reusable para a engine **v1.1.1**.

A `v1.17.0`, cortada hoje, aponta para a **engine v1.1.0 — que está quebrada**. O `npm ci --omit=dev` da composite action falhava com `Missing: esbuild@0.28.2 from lock file` em todo consumidor: o CI da engine validava o lock com npm 11 (via `setup-node`), enquanto a action instala num step de shell com o npm da imagem do runner (**Node 22.23.1 / npm 10.9.8**).

body:
## Summary

Teaches the feature flags runtime client to evaluate the `targets.custom_targets` collection that the API now includes in the `GET /sdk/feature-flags` poll payload behind the `feature-flags-custom-targets` rollout flag (workos/workos#68135). This is stage 4 of the [Custom Targeting Hilltop](https://app.notion.com/p/workos/Hilltop-Custom-Targeting-for-Feature-Flags-391d458aea8b8112a5a3e21e347458c7) rollout plan: ship the runtime contract before typed target management or docs.

### Typed evaluation context

`isEnabled` / `getAllFlags` now accept the Hilltop's direct target-type context map alongside the existing legacy shape:

```ts
// Legacy shape — still supported, normalized internally
client.isEnabled('new-dashboard', { userId: 'user_abc', organizationId: 'org_abc' });

// Typed shape — built-ins and custom types are peers
client.isEnabled('new-dashboard', {
  user: { id: 'user_abc' },
  workspace: { id: 'ws_123' },
});
```

Per the Hilltop's pre-commitments:
- Hybrid contexts (a legacy key alongside a typed resource entry in one call) are rejected rather than given an invented precedence: a warning is logged and no targets match. This is enforced at runtime — the union type does not reject hybrids at compile time (`TypedEvaluationContext`'s index signature makes any key acceptable to the union). Shape detection is by value, not key presence: unset keys and scalar extra fields on a legacy context are ignored, preserving today's behavior for callers passing wider objects.
- Evaluation never throws on invalid context: invalid type keys and IDs (validated with the same rules as the API) log a warning and evaluate as non-matching.
- Target IDs are compared exactly (case-sensitive, no normalization).

### Evaluation semantics aligned with the Hilltop

- Evaluation is enable-only: any enabled target matching the context turns the flag on, with no precedence between target types.
- A target with `enabled: false` is treated as **not present** (falls through to the flag default) instead of forcing the flag off. This field value is reserved for future disabled overrides, per the Hilltop's *Forward compatibility for disabled overrides*. The API only ever writes `enabled: true` today, so this is not an observable behavior change — but it does replace the previous user-over-organization short-circuit, which only mattered for `enabled: false` rows that cannot exist.

### Change detection

`hasEntryChanged` now also diffs `custom_targets`, so a poll cycle where only a custom rule changed emits the `change` event.

### Compatibility

- `targets.custom_targets` is optional in the payload types: polls against servers with the rollout flag off (or older servers) behave exactly as before.
- Until this version is adopted, custom-only flags evaluate to their default on older SDKs — which is why the API keeps the payload gated per team.

## Test plan

- `npx jest src/feature-flags` — 93 tests passing, including new coverage for: exact custom matches, built-in types via the typed form, `enabled: false` treated as absent (including the default-true proof), hybrid-context rejection, unset-key and scalar-extra-field handling, once-per-call warnings in getAllFlags, invalid type/ID warnings, malformed context safety, and a change event fired when only custom targets differ.
- `npm run build` (tsdown + attw + publint) and `npx eslint src/feature-flags` clean.
- Manual: point the client at an environment with the `feature-flags-custom-targets` rollout flag enabled, add a custom rule in the dashboard, and confirm `isEnabled(slug, { <type>: { id } })` flips accordingly.

author: frankyw
body:
## What does this PR do?

`browser_scroll` in Camofox mode doesn't scroll. Two independent problems on the same call path.

### 1. The wheel is inert in headless Firefox

Camofox's `POST /tabs/:id/scroll` calls `page.mouse.wheel()` with the mouse wherever Playwright last left it — **(0,0) on a fresh tab**. In this headless Firefox that wheel event moves nothing.

Measured on a plain document (Wikipedia) and on a JS-rendered app page:

| call | resulting `scrollY` |
|---|---|
| `POST /scroll amount=500` | `0` |
| `POST /scroll amount=2500` | `0` |
| `scrollTo(0, 1234)` via `/evaluate` | `1234` |

So the page and the measurement were both fine — the wheel was simply not doing anything. It isn't free either: it blocks for roughly as long as the travel would take (1.8s at 500px, 6.5s at 2500px) and can reach camofox's 30s handler timeout under load. `/evaluate` does the same job in 3–10ms.

There is no mouse-move endpoint to aim the wheel with, so this is fixed on the client side.

### 2. `browser_scroll` issued five calls per scroll

```python
# Camofox REST API doesn't support pixel args; use repeated calls
_SCROLL_REPEATS = 5
result = None
for _ in range(_SCROLL_REPEATS):
    result = camofox_scroll(direction, task_id)
return result
```

The premise is wrong — camofox's scroll handler destructures `amount`. So the loop bought nothing and cost three things:

- **five HTTP round trips** per tool call, each able to block for the full 30s handler timeout, so one `browser_scroll` could take 150s;
- **intermediate results were overwritten**, so a failure in any iteration but the last was reported as success, and a success after a failure hid the failure;
- **no early exit** — it kept scrolling after a request had already failed.

Observed in the wild: 79.5s of wall clock for a single scroll, containing two 500s, one of them masked by a later success.

## Related Issue

No existing issue found; searched open and closed PRs for `camofox scroll`, `scroll wheel`, `mouse.wheel`.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- **`tools/browser_camofox.py`**
  - `_SCROLL_JS` — scrolls the document, falling back to the largest genuinely-scrollable container for pages that pin the document at 0, and reporting whether anything moved.
  - `camofox_scroll` gains an optional `amount` (default 500, matching camofox's own default) and goes through `/evaluate`.
  - The payload now carries `at` and `height`, plus `at_end: True` when nothing moved. **Reaching the bottom stays `success: True`** on purpose — it is a normal outcome, and reporting it as an error teaches agents to retry a scroll that is already done.
- **`tools/browser_tool.py`** — one call passing `amount` instead of the five-call loop. Total travel is preserved deliberately (five notches × camofox's 500px default), so agents that scroll N times to reach content behave exactly as before rather than suddenly needing five times as many calls.
- **`tests/tools/test_browser_camofox.py`** — a `TestCamofoxScroll` class (there was none; `camofox_scroll` was imported by two test modules and exercised by neither).

## How to Test

1. `pytest tests/tools/test_browser_camofox.py -q` → 24 passed.
2. Revert both tool files and re-run `-k Scroll`: 3 of the 4 new tests fail. They are real regression tests.
3. Against a live Camofox, on any long page:
   ```
   browser_navigate("https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scrolling")
   browser_scroll("down")
   browser_snapshot()
   ```
   Before: the snapshot is unchanged and the call takes seconds. After: the page has moved and `at`/`height` report where it is.

## Note on #54890

That open PR adds a 404 guard to `camofox_scroll` (among seven other functions). This PR rewrites the body of the same function, so they will conflict textually. The two changes are independent in substance and I'm happy to rebase whichever lands second.

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)

- [x] I've added tests for my changes

> **On the full suite:** all 64 tests across the seven `test_browser_camofox*.py` files pass. I could not run `pytest tests/ -q` in full — unrelated modules fail to *collect* in my environment for missing optional deps (`aiohttp`, `httpx`, `mcp`, `rich`, `websockets`), which this change doesn't touch.

### Documentation & Housekeeping

body:
## What changed

Adds ADR-0005 accepting `Files` as a Project-scoped shared asset layer for MOZG.

The ADR fixes the key boundaries before implementation:

- Files is a standalone Project-scoped persistence domain.
- Current Product Project identity follows the accepted Desktop Snapshot V3 contract: `project_id text`, not a foreign key to the currently-unused `public.projects` UUID table.
- A separate private `project-files` bucket is the target Storage boundary.
- Originals remain immutable user assets; previews/edge variants are derived caches.
- Object keys are stable and independent of folder names and user filenames.
- Folder rename/move is metadata-only.
- Storage access is authorized from authoritative metadata + workspace roles, not path parsing alone.
- Files receives its own MIME/size policy rather than inheriting the Canvas 20 MB/image-only limit.
- Deletion is soft by default.
- Cross-domain reuse is by `file_id`, not by copying physical binaries.
- Rollout remains staged: standalone Files → Files-to-Canvas → new Canvas uploads through Files → legacy Canvas migration evaluation last.

## Why

The current Canvas asset pipeline already preserves originals and produces efficient derived image variants, but `canvas_assets` is Canvas-owned. Generalizing that table directly would couple all files to Canvas. Building a permanently separate file store would create duplicate physical assets when the same image is used by Canvas, Tasks or Knowledge.

The ADR establishes Files as the future common asset identity while keeping the existing Canvas system untouched during Stage A.

## Impact

Documentation only. No Production code, schema, Storage bucket, RLS policy or user data is changed by this PR.

## Validation

- Checked current Production schema and bucket configuration read-only.
- Verified current Canvas/Canvas-group project scope uses opaque text Project ids.
- Verified `public.projects` currently has no Production rows, so Files must not introduce a UUID Project FK at this checkpoint.
- Confirmed existing ADR numbering; ADR-0005 is the next slot.

## Acceptance

Accepted by the product owner on 2026-08-14; implementation proceeds in separate Stage A foundation work.

## Next step

A separate Stage A foundation PR updates `ARCHITECTURE.md`, creates the schema/bucket through a Supabase CLI migration, regenerates DB types, adds RLS/Storage tests and implements the typed Files repository boundary.

body:
## O que muda

Os concluídos eram uma pílula na barra de filtros da lista de trabalho — mas quem procura um caso arquivado sabe o nome, não a posição numa lista. E a pílula trocava o conteúdo da tela inteira para isso.

### Na lateral

O Arquivo passa a ser item da lateral, fechando a lista das etapas — é o fim da esteira, depois que o caso sai dela. Vem separado por um fio para não se confundir com etapa ativa, e com a contagem de arquivados ao lado.

### O modal

Clicar abre um modal com **busca por nome, tipo de ato, ação e observação**, listando do mais recém-concluído para o mais antigo, com a data de conclusão em cada linha.

Clicar num resultado fecha o modal e leva ao **card** — que é onde mora o botão "Reabrir", e onde se decide retomar de verdade.

### A faixa de volta

A pílula sai da barra, e no lugar dela entra uma faixa que só aparece quando a lista está mostrando o arquivo: sem pílula, nada indicaria que a lista deixou de mostrar os ativos, nem como voltar. Ela some sozinha quando o filtro volta.

Isso também cobre um comportamento que já existia e acontecia sem aviso: quando uma busca na tela principal só encontra resultado entre os concluídos, o painel pula para o arquivo sozinho.

## Como foi verificado

Painel carregado num navegador com o SDK do Firebase substituído por um stub e 4 casos concluídos.

- **Lateral:** "Arquivo" é o último item de `#sidebar-etapas`, logo após "Nota de exigência", com a classe de separação e a contagem 4.
- **Barra de filtros:** a pílula "Arquivo" já não está entre os filtros; a faixa "Arquivo · voltar aos ativos" começa oculta (`display:none`).
- **Modal:** subtítulo "4 casos concluídos" e os 4 listados na ordem certa, cada um com tipo e data de conclusão.
- **Busca:** "toledo" reduz a lista a 1 e o subtítulo passa a "1 de 4 casos".
- **Caminho até o card:** clicar num resultado fecha o modal, traz o card à tela, o card mostra o botão "Reabrir", e a faixa de volta acende (`display:flex`).
- Balanço de chaves do CSS zerado, `node --check` no módulo JS, sem erros de console.

## Pedido (RD-41 · BPO/Financeiro · Jordana · evolução do #983)

"Não precisar informar qual remessa — o `.RET` pode ter pagamentos de várias remessas; o sistema deve buscar nos títulos os boletos que devem ser baixados."

Tira o passo "selecionar a remessa". O sistema casa cada pagamento do `.RET` **direto com o título**, por identificador, **atravessando todas as remessas** — nunca pelo número do arquivo (NSA), nunca exigindo seleção.

## Parte A — RPC de auto-conciliação (`fn_remessa_retorno_conciliar_auto`)

`(p_company_id, p_itens jsonb, p_confirmar boolean)`, SECURITY DEFINER, GRANT a `authenticated`.

- **Casamento por identificador:** boleto pelo **código de barras** (único → casa sozinho, como no #983); PIX/documento por `chave_pix`/`numero_documento` **+ valor do título**. Atravessa todas as remessas não-canceladas da empresa.
- **Baixa** via `fn_pagar_baixar_pagamento` (mesma baixa canônica do resto · RD-52); item → `status_item='pago'`.
- **Idempotência ancorada no título** (`erp_pagar.status='pago'`) **e no item** (`status_item='pago'`): reimportar o mesmo `.RET` → `ja_pago`, **0 baixas novas** — à prova de qualquer caminho de baixa.
- **Segurança (RD-38):** só baixa pagamento **confirmado** pelo banco (com data + valor pago > 0). Linha de **rejeição** (sem data/valor) casa o título mas **não** baixa → `rejeitado`.
- Não casa a mesma linha 2× na execução. Retorno honesto (RD-51 · 3 estados): `casados` / `rejeitados` / `ja_pagos` / `nao_casados` + `resumo`.

> **Desvio anotado do rascunho da SPEC:** o rascunho usava `status_item='baixado'`, mas o **check constraint** de `status_item` só aceita `incluido/enviado/pago/rejeitado/pendente`. Usei **`'pago'`** (o mesmo estado terminal do fluxo por-remessa `fn_remessa_retorno_processar`) — evita split-brain e passa no banco.

## Parte B — Tela (`remessa-pagamento`)

- **Removido o dropdown de remessa.** Fluxo: sobe o `.RET` → auto-conciliação (prévia, não grava) → **Confirmar baixa**.
- Prévia mostra **casados** (título · remessa Nº · valor · ocorrência), **rejeitados** (casaram título mas o banco não confirmou), **já baixados** e **não casados** (pagamentos sem título — a Jordana trata manual). O NSA do arquivo vira **só referência**.

## Parte C — Validação (RD-38, transação revertida em produção)

`.RET` com pagamentos de **2 remessas** (9991, 9992) + 1 linha de rejeição + 1 sem título:
- **Prévia:** 2 a baixar · 1 rejeitado · 1 não-casado ✓
- **Confirmar:** 2 títulos baixados, de **2 remessas distintas** (multi-remessa) ✓; o item rejeitado **NÃO** foi baixado (título segue aberto) ✓
- **Reimportar:** 0 novos · 2 já-pagos (idempotente) ✓

Migração aplicada em produção via MCP (o CEO autoriza DDL). `tsc` ✅ · `eslint` ✅ · build **✓ Compiled successfully / Finished TypeScript** (falha só na rota pré-existente `/api/assessor/analisar-erp`, limitação de env local).

## Guardas

- [x] Casa por identificador do título (barra/chave+valor), atravessa remessas — nunca pelo número do arquivo nem exige seleção.
- [x] RD-52: baixa via `fn_pagar_baixar_pagamento`, item marcado `pago`.
- [x] Idempotente: título/item já pago → `ja_pago`, impede baixa dupla na reimportação.
- [x] Pilar 3: Jordana só sobe o arquivo e confirma; o sistema acha os títulos.
- [x] RD-38: casamento multi-remessa + baixa + idempotência provados.

## Prova operacional (com você/Jordana)

Subir o `6YT612081734.RET` real (sem escolher remessa) → conferir os casados/não-casados → confirmar → eu confiro no banco: títulos baixados, itens `status_item='pago'` + `ocorrencia_retorno`; e a contra-prova de reimportação.

author: andyleejordan
body:
Adds a managed `copy-issue-labels.yml` workflow to `terraform/root`, so every AVM Terraform module repository copies the release-note labels from a merged pull request's closing issues onto the pull request itself.

## Why

GitHub builds release notes from **pull request** labels, but AVM triage puts the category label on the **issue**. So a pull request that closes a triaged issue lands in the uncategorized bucket unless someone relabels it by hand. In `Azure/terraform-azurerm-avm-res-network-virtualnetwork`, none of the last fifteen merged pull requests carries a single label, so today that bucket is where nearly everything ends up.

## Trigger

It runs on `push` to `main`, not on the pull request.

- **`pull_request_target` is not used.** It runs with a writable token in the base repository's context and has been flagged repeatedly in MSRC cases.
- **`pull_request` cannot cover forks.** `GITHUB_TOKEN` is read-only for *every* `pull_request` activity type on a fork pull request, including `closed`, so it could not apply labels. Roughly 10% of merges here are fork pull requests, so that is not an acceptable gap.
- **`push` to `main` avoids both problems.** It always runs in the trusted base-repository context, never executes contributor code, and treats fork and non-fork pull requests identically.

Labeling after the merge is still in time: release notes read pull request labels when the release is created.

## Implementation

Three `gh` calls, in the order the problem is stated:

1. **Find the pull request.** `GET /repos/{repo}/commits/{sha}/pulls` returns the pull requests associated with the pushed commit, along with each one's merge state, base branch, **and labels**. Squash, merge, and rebase merges all associate the pull request with this commit.
2. **Stop if it is already categorized.** The labels from step 1 are intersected against the allowlist with `grep -Fxf`. A pull request the author already labeled is left alone, and no issue is fetched.
3. **Otherwise copy from the closing issues.** `gh pr view --json closingIssuesReferences`, then `gh issue view --json labels`, intersected against the same allowlist and applied in a single `gh pr edit --add-label`.

`gh` is used rather than raw REST for the write because it takes every label in one call, handles names like `Type: Bug :bug:` without quoting hazards, and *refuses* to add a label the repository does not have. The underlying REST `addLabels` endpoint silently **creates** unknown labels instead — verified against this repository, which returned 200 and created a grey `ededed` label. Left unguarded that would scatter placeholder labels across every module repository.

## Behavior worth calling out

- **The allowlist is exactly the labels `release.yml` sorts into a category.** The `exclude:` labels (`dependencies`, `github-actions`, `github_actions`) are deliberately absent: copying one onto a pull request would drop it from the release notes altogether rather than sort it, which is worse than leaving it uncategorized.
- **Squash is the only merge these repositories allow**, so the pushed commit belongs to exactly one pull request — confirmed across 25 consecutive commits on a module repository's `main`, each returning exactly one. Both conditions on it are still checked: `merged_at` because the endpoint also reports a pull request that merely *contains* the commit and has not merged (verified against this pull request), and `base.ref` because it is redundant only for as long as `allow_merge_commit` stays off, which is a repository setting rather than an invariant.
- **Closing issues in another repository are skipped**, since their labels need not exist here.
- **Nothing is ever removed, and an existing label is never overwritten.** The workflow only ever adds.
- **No `|| true` anywhere except one `grep` that is expected to match nothing.** Every API failure fails the job.
- **No concurrency group, deliberately.** GitHub keeps only one *pending* run per group, so a third rapid push would evict the second and its pull request would never be labeled. Each run only touches its own commit's pull request, so overlapping runs are harmless.

## Validation

- YAML parses and `bash -n` is clean.
- A stubbed-`gh` harness asserts on the exact `gh pr edit` argv across twelve cases: a category copied from the closing issue, AVM `Status:`/`Needs:` labels ignored, an `exclude:` label never copied, an issue with no category, several categories in one call, de-duplication across two closing issues, a pull request already labeled, a non-category label not counting as labeled, a closing issue in another repository, a pull request merged into another branch, a push that merged no pull request, and a pull request that closes no issue.
- The script was then run unstubbed against real merge commits in this repository, exercising the live API payloads through both the short-circuit and the no-category paths.
- `gh pr edit --add-label` was confirmed end-to-end against this pull request, adding and then removing a label.

## Note on the earlier revisions

This branch spent a few commits on an `actions/github-script` implementation. It was dropped: it came to roughly twice the size, and most of the extra code existed only to re-implement label handling that `gh` provides for free. It also would have added a SHA-pinned action dependency to every module repository, and this repository's Dependabot `github-actions` glob does not match any file group (#18), so it would never have been updated. The correctness fixes found along the way were kept.

## Prior art

Three community actions do something similar. None fits:

- [`michalvankodev/copy-issue-labels`](https://github.com/michalvankodev/copy-issue-labels) (7 stars) — built for `pull_request: opened`, so a fork pull request's read-only token cannot apply labels.
- [`williambdean/closing-labels`](https://github.com/williambdean/closing-labels) (3 stars) — built for `pull_request_target`, and is a Docker action that builds from its `Dockerfile` on every run.
- [`laurelmay/copy-issue-labels`](https://github.com/laurelmay/copy-issue-labels) (0 stars) — `pull_request_target`, last released in 2022.

The first is the closest: it accepts an explicit `issue-number`, so it could be driven from a push workflow, and its `labels-to-include` matches the allowlist here. But it only takes a pull request number and reads the issues linked from that pull request's body. It does not resolve commit to merged pull request, which is the part that lets this run on `push` instead of `pull_request_target`. Adopting it would mean keeping that step anyway and adding a single-maintainer dependency that ships a committed `dist/index.js` into every module repository.
